meta.title: Pakistani General Elections
sources: Wikipedia: Pakistani general election articles 1962-2024 (results tables and infoboxes)
Election Commission of Pakistan figures as reported there

eras.label: Basic Democracies
eras.blurb: Ayub Khan's 1962 constitution had the National Assembly chosen not by voters but by an electoral college of eighty thousand Basic Democrats, themselves elected in the union councils. Political parties were banned outright for the 1962 election and readmitted for 1965, and both assemblies were dominated by the president's Convention Muslim League.

eras.label: One person, one vote
eras.blurb: The 1970 election was the first held on universal adult suffrage anywhere in Pakistan's history, and it broke the country: the Awami League won 167 of the 313 seats on an entirely East Pakistani vote, the result was not honoured, and Bangladesh was independent within a year. The 1977 election that followed gave Bhutto a landslide his opponents refused to accept, and the army removed him in July.

eras.label: Under Zia
eras.blurb: Eight years of martial law produced one election, held on a nonpartisan basis with candidates standing as individuals and amendments written to keep the opposition off the ballot. The Movement for the Restoration of Democracy boycotted it. Almost every member returned supported the regime.

eras.label: The democratic decade
eras.blurb: Four elections in nine years and not one of the assemblies they produced served a full term: Benazir Bhutto and Nawaz Sharif alternated twice each, and every government in between was dismissed by a president using the powers Zia had left behind. Turnout fell at every election of the period, to 35.8% in 1997.

eras.label: Under Musharraf
eras.blurb: The 1999 coup was followed three years later by an election held under a president who had granted himself the power to dissolve the assembly, with the two main party leaders in exile and a graduation requirement that disqualified most of the political class. A new pro-government Muslim League came first.

eras.label: The civilian era
eras.blurb: Since 2008 every National Assembly has handed over to the next, which had never happened before, and every one of those elections has been contested as unfair by the side that lost. Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf came first in 2018 and, stripped of its party symbol by the courts, again in 2024 with its candidates standing as independents.

elections.summary: A pakistani election; the results table for this contest is not on file.
elections.caveat: Political parties were banned and the election was held on a non-partisan basis, with the Assembly chosen indirectly by the Basic Democracies electoral college.

elections.summary: Convention Muslim League finished first with 120 of 156 seats. Ayub Khan stayed in office.
elections.caveat: The Assembly was elected indirectly by the Basic Democracies electoral college, whose own members had been chosen in October and November 1964.

elections.summary: All-Pakistan Awami League finished first with 167 of 313 seats on 39.2% of the vote. Turnout 58.0%.
Pakistan Peoples Party finished first with 171 of 216 seats on 59.7% of the vote. Zulfikar Ali Bhutto stayed in office.
elections.caveat: The Pakistan National Alliance accused the Pakistan Peoples Party of rigging the result and refused to accept it, and the source files this election under electoral fraud in Pakistan.

elections.summary: Independents finished first with 217 of 237 seats on 100.0% of the vote. Turnout 53.7%. Muhammad Khan Junejo replaced None.
elections.caveat: Held under Zia-ul-Haq's military government on a nonpartisan basis, with amendments to the Political Parties Act written to disqualify opposition candidates; the Movement for the Restoration of Democracy boycotted, and most of those returned supported the regime.

elections.summary: Pakistan Peoples Party finished first with 93 of 237 seats on 37.7% of the vote. Turnout 42.8%. Benazir Bhutto replaced None (presidential rule).
Islami Jamhoori Ittehad finished first with 106 of 217 seats on 36.5% of the vote. Turnout 45.2%. Nawaz Sharif replaced Benazir Bhutto.
Pakistan Peoples Party finished first with 89 of 217 seats on 37.0% of the vote. Turnout 40.0%. Benazir Bhutto replaced Nawaz Sharif.
Pakistan Muslim League (N) finished first with 135 of 217 seats on 44.9% of the vote. Turnout 35.8%. Nawaz Sharif replaced Benazir Bhutto.
Pakistan Muslim League (Q) finished first with 105 of 342 seats on 25.7% of the vote. Turnout 41.8%. Zafarullah Khan Jamali replaced Pervez Musharraf (as Chief Executive).
Pakistan Peoples Party finished first with 116 of 342 seats on 30.8% of the vote. Turnout 44.3%. Yousaf Raza Gillani replaced Shaukat Aziz.
Pakistan Muslim League (N) finished first with 166 of 342 seats on 32.8% of the vote. Turnout 55.0%. Nawaz Sharif replaced Raja Pervez Ashraf.
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf finished first with 151 of 342 seats on 31.8% of the vote. Turnout 51.7%. Imran Khan replaced Shahid Khaqan Abbasi.
elections.caveat: The European Union observer mission reported systematic attempts to undermine the ruling party, a lack of equality of opportunity, pressure on the media and judicial conduct that had all negatively influenced the campaign.

elections.summary: Pakistan Muslim League (N) finished first with 98 of 336 seats on 23.6% of the vote. Turnout 47.8%. Shehbaz Sharif took office.
elections.caveat: A Supreme Court ruling stripped Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf of its electoral symbol before the vote, so its candidates stood as independents, and the party's website and voter helpline were blocked in the country.
